spans.title: The Earl and the Bull
spans.blurb: A timid young clerk hears shouting from a pasture: an elderly earl is holding off a charging bull with nothing but a garden spud.

spans.title: The Man Who Called Himself Farr
spans.blurb: A sunburnt stranger in vagrant's clothes strolls a June road, baffling a constable, rescuing a stalled motorcar, and trading looks with a girl who remembers to say please.

spans.title: The Dandelion Clock
spans.blurb: Alone by the bridge, a girl blows dandelion seeds to divine a stranger's age. On the very last puff, a shadow falls across the grass.

spans.title: The Eve of Waterloo
spans.blurb: Brussels dances by lamplight, a thousand hearts beating happily, when a deep sound rolls in from the distance. Some say it is only the wind.

spans.title: The Sacred Goose
spans.blurb: Three sacred geese ambush a temple guest, and he fights back with a table leg. The priestess returns to find her darling dead and her house polluted.

spans.title: The Widow of Ephesus
spans.blurb: A widow famed for devotion vows to starve in her husband's tomb. Nearby, a soldier guarding crucified thieves notices a light among the graves.

spans.title: Da Capo!
spans.blurb: After a rehearsal so wretched he nearly stays home, a young composer goes to his symphony's premiere, resolved to seize the first violin himself if things go wrong.

spans.title: Shelter from the Storm
spans.blurb: A sudden storm drives three drenched walkers to a bachelor's gate. He lights the kitchen fire, pours brandy, and hands round tea while the thunder does its work.

spans.title: A Wedding in the Dark
spans.blurb: On a quiet Sunday evening a young governess learns her wedding is to happen at once, in a darkened room, to a bridegroom who cannot bear the light.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that the heroine's secret marriage to the unseen recluse takes place, a mid-book development, though the deeper mystery of the bridegroom stays intact.

spans.title: The Undoer of Wrongs
spans.blurb: A knight-errant follows cries into a thicket, where a farmer flogs a shepherd boy. Justice is pronounced, sworn to, and left to keep itself.
